subject: getting scale.model right for interpreting parameters

messages.author: bbb9357156c132fe
messages.subject: getting scale.model right for interpreting parameters
parts:
Hi everyone,
If I use scale.model=TRUE on a random walk 2, is it correct to say that the precision that is outputted isn't scaled? (ie the option just effects the choice of prior?)

If so, how do I get the posterior of the precision of the scaled component out?

(This question bought to you by a standard deviation parameter [transformed from the quantiles of the precision] of O(30) but a RW2 that deviates from zero of O(1)).

Thanks!

Dan

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] getting scale.model right for interpreting parameters
parts:
Hi,

the scale.model=TRUE implementation is done slightly different than in
the 'scaling intrinsic' paper. Instead of scaling the prior, the model
itself it scaled so to have marginal variance about 1, when precision =
1. If you got some weird results, its likely some other reason for it.

H

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] getting scale.model right for interpreting parameters
parts:
Have you removed the linear term for the RW2 and added it as a separate component of the model? This is the interpretation of the precision parameter.

Haakon
